stories.body: Two people were killed and eight wounded when a Houthi attack struck King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, while two others died after Saudi air defences intercepted a drone targeting Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield. The Iran-aligned Houthis said they had also targeted other Saudi airports, the defence ministry and Aramco facilities, as Saudi Arabia and its allies reported intercepting additional drones. Reports that Aramco evacuated staff from its Dhahran headquarters, alongside Iranian claims of attacks on vessels in the Gulf and mines near the Strait of Hormuz, heightened concern about energy supplies: Brent crude rose 3% to about $112 a barrel, its highest level since May.
stories.headline: Iran-linked attacks in Saudi Arabia kill four and push oil to a five-month high

stories.body: Russia and Ukraine traded large drone and missile attacks hours after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg and said Moscow had agreed in principle to resume talks with Kyiv and Washington after 10 November. Ukrainian authorities said Russian strikes on Kyiv killed at least two people and wounded 22, damaging homes, energy infrastructure, a bridge, an ambulance station and other sites; Moscow said it intercepted 630 Ukrainian drones aimed at the Russian capital. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the use of ballistic missiles, including cluster munitions, demonstrated that Russia was not serious about peace and called for stronger air defences and sanctions.
stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine exchange major strikes as Moscow agrees to resume trilateral talks

stories.body: President Emmanuel Macron said demonstrations called by people or groups without recognised authority would be prohibited in the coming days, while union-backed marches could proceed under legal conditions and with altered routes. The measures follow violent cost-of-living protests and looting last weekend, which Macron blamed in part on people seeking to loot and on ultra-left groups seeking to destabilise the state. Authorities have already imposed restrictions in Lyon, Marseille, Nice and Toulon, and a Paris march has been barred from entering the city centre; Macron is due to convene a defence council to decide further measures before planned Saturday demonstrations.
stories.headline: Macron seeks to ban unauthorised protests after violent unrest in France

stories.body: Two newly disclosed vulnerabilities in PHP, the language that underpins a large share of the web and platforms including WordPress, have prompted hosting providers and site operators to apply emergency mitigations and patches. Researchers found the flaws with assistance from advanced AI models and had planned a coordinated disclosure while fixes were prepared, but news leaked before the patch window was complete. There are no confirmed successful attacks, though security firms have recorded millions of attempted exploits; authorities and experts are urging owners to update immediately, with older PHP installations needing upgrades before they can receive the relevant fix.
stories.headline: Major PHP vulnerabilities put millions of websites at risk

stories.body: French authorities have identified the first documented human infection with Shamonda virus, a midge-borne virus previously known mainly in livestock such as cattle, sheep and goats. The patient, who had a severely compromised immune system and died in early October, experienced neurological complications that officials believe were very likely linked to the infection, although investigations continue into its role in the death and how it was acquired. French, European and World Health Organization officials say the case appears exceptional, there is no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission, and the current risk to the public is low.
stories.headline: France reports first known human case of Shamonda virus

stories.body: Wedgewood Polls admitted that it fabricated its polling data after being confronted by the polling-analysis site FiftyPlusOne, raising questions about how false surveys entered campaign coverage and polling aggregators. Its polls were cited by outlets including The New York Times and Politico and may have affected donor confidence, volunteer morale and narratives in several races. Michigan Democrat Mallory McMorrow said a false poll showing her support collapsing helped dry up donations and contributed to her exit from the Senate primary, while other Wedgewood surveys were promoted in races in Wisconsin and Mississippi. The episode has intensified concerns that unverified polling can distort political strategy, prediction markets and public perceptions in future primaries.
stories.headline: Fake polling firm may have influenced midterm narratives and campaign decisions

stories.body: Across more than two dozen statewide debates, Democratic candidates repeatedly tied Republicans to President Donald Trump and blamed tariffs and the war with Iran for higher fuel and consumer costs, while Republican candidates varied in how closely they embraced the president. Candidates in several states also found rare bipartisan common ground in opposing or restricting data-centre development, favouring local control and safeguards against higher utility bills. The campaign debates also exposed a broader decline in the practice, with major-party candidates in several competitive states declining invitations or failing to agree on formats.
stories.headline: Midterm debates put affordability, Iran and data centres at the centre of state races

stories.body: Republicans have spent substantially more than Democrats on broadcast advertising in 10 key Senate battleground states, but much of that advantage is diluted because GOP spending relies more heavily on outside groups, which pay higher rates than campaigns and political parties. Republican groups have spent $677 million versus $479 million for Democrats, yet in states including Ohio, Texas and Michigan their spending share has translated into only a modestly larger share of ads on air. Strong Democratic candidate fundraising and lower candidate rates have helped offset Republican super-PAC money, while some GOP strategists say late reservations by Trump-aligned MAGA Inc. made airtime even more expensive.
stories.headline: Democrats' lower ad rates blunt Republicans' television spending advantage

stories.body: Spain's Socialist Party has accepted a four-candidate election debate on RTVE on 26 November and a head-to-head debate between Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Popular Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo on private media on 16 November. The PSOE says both events are indispensable and has accused the PP of trying to veto the public broadcaster, while the parties remain divided over the venue for the four-way contest, which would also include Vox and Frente Amplio. The agreements come less than 40 days before the 29 November general election.
stories.headline: Sánchez accepts four-way RTVE debate and a head-to-head with Feijóo

stories.body: The Popular Party has released an AI-generated campaign video that imitates the images and voices of Socialist leaders and people connected to the government, making them appear to admit to alleged wrongdoing. The video, branded "Lerdos y orgullosos," parodies a real Pedro Sánchez campaign video that reclaimed the insult "zurdos" for the left. PSOE spokesperson Rebeca Torró condemned the production as lamentable and said the PP was extending a strategy of personal attacks and falsehoods; reporting described it as the first known use by a Spanish political party of AI to impersonate political figures in this way.
stories.headline: Spain's PP uses AI-generated videos impersonating Socialist figures

stories.body: Spain and Italy have agreed not to extend the reciprocal border controls imposed on flights and passenger sea links after the Ceuta migration crisis in late July. Italy introduced checks in early August in response to the arrival of thousands of migrants in Ceuta from Morocco, and Spain retaliated with comparable controls on travellers arriving from Italy. Following talks between Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, the countries' interior ministers agreed to restore normal Schengen movement while strengthening information-sharing and other security cooperation.
stories.headline: Spain and Italy agree to lift border controls imposed during Ceuta crisis

stories.body: Spanish National Police found 74 migrants living in overcrowded and precarious conditions in an apartment in Ceuta's El Príncipe neighbourhood, including 54 men, 10 women and 10 unaccompanied minors. Police arrested a Ceuta resident suspected of leading a criminal network that housed migrants while awaiting opportunities to move them illegally to mainland Spain. Investigators say some minors may have suffered physical abuse, including dog bites, and are examining alleged labour exploitation of both children and adults.
stories.headline: Police find 74 migrants, including 10 children, overcrowded in Ceuta apartment

stories.body: Spain's transport minister, Óscar Puente, and Catalan president Salvador Illa said the transfer of the R1 Rodalies line is irreversible and could be completed soon, with the relevant bilateral commission expected to meet before the 29 November general election. Puente said a new Renfe programme contract, setting services and annual financial obligations of roughly €460 million through 2028, is scheduled for approval next Tuesday. The R1, which connects Barcelona through the Maresme to Maçanet-Massanes, is intended to be the first infrastructure transfer in the broader Rodalies de Catalunya arrangement, whose joint operating company is expected to begin service in 2027.
stories.headline: Catalonia's planned transfer of the R1 commuter-rail line moves toward signature

stories.body: Barcelona accounts for 32 of Spain's 100 most expensive rental areas, according to the latest National Statistics Institute figures, which cover 2024. Pedralbes ranks as the city's costliest area at an average monthly rent of €2,002, second nationally only to Madrid's Recoletos, while Tres Torres averages €1,911. A separate analysis finds that rent and utilities consume an average 35.3% of household income in Barcelona, rising to 47.4% in Ciutat Vella; the commonly cited affordability threshold is 30%.
stories.headline: Barcelona holds 32 of Spain's 100 most expensive rental areas

stories.body: Around 50 companies in Barcelona's cruise sector have issued a manifesto rejecting the city government's plan to raise the tourist tax for stopover cruise passengers to €30 by 2030. The industry says the measure unfairly discriminates against it and objects to using taxation to reduce cruise activity, while calling on Mayor Jaume Collboni for dialogue on a more balanced and environmentally respectful future for the sector. Under the phased increase approved in September, passengers staying less than 12 hours would see their current combined €11 charge rise gradually from 2027.
stories.headline: Barcelona cruise sector opposes planned €30 tax on short-stop passengers

stories.body: Catalonia's Platform for Media Education has called on the Generalitat to make media and information literacy a lasting public-policy priority, with a stable strategy to counter disinformation and strengthen critical thinking. At a Barcelona conference during UNESCO's Global Media and Information Literacy Week, the coalition of about 50 education and communications organisations presented a manifesto advocating training not only in schools but also for adults, older people and groups especially vulnerable to digital and information gaps. Speakers warned that algorithmic platforms, misinformation and polarisation are affecting democratic and electoral processes.
stories.headline: Barcelona media-literacy platform calls for permanent strategy against disinformation
